research: Kd's research file, "Normal Squat (Bodyweight Squat) Guide" (his folder, squat normal), its eleven common mistakes; and the Library's source for the squat, ACE's Exercise Library: Bodyweight Squat.

mistakes.name: Leaning too far forward
mistakes.source: Research file: "Leaning too far forward: this shifts the load to the lower back. Keep your chest up." Its key angles: torso lean moderate, about 30 to 45 degrees forward from vertical.

standard.source: Research file, key angles: torso lean moderate, about 30 to 45 degrees forward from vertical.

coach.silent: No published source gives a fixed lean as a mistake: the research file's 30 to 45 degrees is a usual range, and Myer et al. 2014 (Strength Cond J), the trunk about parallel to the shins, reads proper squats of three people up to 20.8 degrees past it, its line 12 to 25 with one person left out (measured 2026-11-27). Spoken once Kd rules it or more side-on bodies set it (54).

mistakes.from: Set by form-check: the further out of the form standard, 45 (its source beside it), and the furthest proper rep that reads it, as filmed and as each replay that sets numbers (40.06; 14 reps as filmed, 3 people), plus the camera's own room: the same rep's change from as filmed to each such replay, in 99 reps of 100 (126 reps): 0.41; rounded outward.

mistakes.name: Hips rising before the chest
mistakes.source: Research file: "Hips rising before the chest: this turns the lift into a stiff-legged hinge. Rise with your hips and chest together."
mistakes.why: From a phone on the floor a man's own proper squats read the chest 3.1 to 4.2 degrees further forward half way out of the bottom than at it (once 12.6), as filmed and replayed; a line set from the eight others alone, all filmed from hip height, lies at 3 degrees and marks his proper squats. He is the only person filmed from the floor: tried again with more floor bodies (jobs 53 and 54).

mistakes.name: Knees shooting far forward with the hips staying high
mistakes.source: Research file: "Knees shooting far forward with the hips staying high: start the movement by sending the hips back." Its key angles: shin angle a slight forward lean, about 15 to 30 degrees.
mistakes.why: Read side on, the shins' lean less the thighs' at the bottom: a man's own proper squats, from the floor and a raised phone, read -17 to -29 degrees; the eight others' reach -32 at most, and a line set from them alone, -30, marks his proper squats. Tried again with more bodies (jobs 53 and 54).

mistakes.name: Knees caving inward
mistakes.source: Research file: "Knees caving inward: this stresses the knee ligaments. Push your knees out over your toes." ACE: keep your knees in line with your second toes.

coach.words: Keep your knees in line with your toes.

standard.source: ACE: keep your knees in line with your second toes; the research file: let your knees track outward over your toes. So the knees never come closer together, against the feet, than they stood.

mistakes.from: Set by form-check: the further out of the form standard, 0 (its source beside it), and the furthest proper rep that reads it, as filmed and as each replay that sets numbers (-0.02; 17 reps as filmed, 6 people), minus the camera's own room: the same rep's change from as filmed to each such replay, in 99 reps of 100 (148 reps): 0.1; rounded outward.

mistakes.name: Quarter reps
mistakes.source: Research file: "Quarter reps: very shallow squats limit glute and hamstring work. Go to parallel if your mobility allows."

mistakes.name: Feet shifting during the set
mistakes.source: ACE (the Library's squat file): keep both feet planted in one place.

mistakes.name: Heels lifting
mistakes.source: Research file: "Heels lifting: this usually points to tight ankles and puts extra load on the knees. Keep your whole foot planted." ACE: heels lift off the floor.
mistakes.why: On proper squats the heel point alone reads up to 11.5 cm above where it stood, its toes down, from a phone on the floor (5.3 in the middle), and up to 5.1 cm from hip height (4.2 in 95 of 100): a heel lifted less than that cannot be told from the pose model's own wander (measured 2026-11-22, 72 feet of 43 reps).

mistakes.name: Bouncing out of the bottom
mistakes.source: Research file: "Bouncing out of the bottom: this uses momentum instead of muscle control."
mistakes.why: Proper squats in the videos stay at the bottom for as little as 0.10 s (0.17 s in 5 of 100), three pictures at 30 a second: a bounce is as short, and the muscles let go are not in the body's points, so it cannot be told from a brisk proper squat (measured 2026-11-22, 43 reps).

mistakes.name: Rounding the lower back
mistakes.source: Research file: "Rounding the lower back (butt wink): stop the descent just before your pelvis tucks under." ACE: back rounds at the bottom.
mistakes.why: The pose model gives no point along the spine or on the pelvis, only the shoulders and the hips, so the back's own shape is not in what it sees.

mistakes.name: Locking the knees hard at the top
mistakes.source: Research file: "Locking the knees hard at the top: this jars the joint."
mistakes.why: A knee's angle reads 180 degrees at its straightest and never past it, and how hard a joint locks is a force, not a place the camera sees.

mistakes.name: Holding your breath for the whole rep
mistakes.source: Research file: "Holding your breath for the whole rep: brace on the way down and exhale on the way up."
mistakes.why: Breathing is not a movement of the body's points.

mistakes.name: Feet too narrow or too wide
mistakes.source: Research file: "Feet too narrow or too wide: too narrow limits balance and depth; too wide shifts the work to the inner thighs and turns it into a sumo squat."
mistakes.why: A wide stance is the sumo squat's own, a twin of this movement whose videos set its numbers: set with the squat's twins, each its own exercise (job 54).
